# llms.txt — Context for AI Agents

This file exists so any AI assistant (Claude or otherwise) picking up this
project — in a new chat, a different tool, or a different model — can get
oriented quickly without the human having to re-explain everything from
scratch. If you are an AI reading this: read this whole file before doing
anything. If you are Dev reading this: see HUMAN_QUICKSTART.md in this same
folder for the short version to paste into a new chat.

Last updated: 2026-08-13

## What this project is

An automated content pipeline for the Instagram/X/Threads/Pinterest account
`@the_higher_being` — daily philosophy quotes and psychology facts, plus a
twice-weekly long-form "essay" series pairing philosophers' claims with real
modern research. Everything runs unattended via GitHub Actions. There is no
Make.com, no manual posting step, no human in the loop for routine operation.

The account is genuinely early-stage (near-zero followers as of this
writing). The whole point of this build is consistency the human couldn't
sustain manually, feeding into a funnel: social posts -> a self-hosted
link-in-bio page -> a free lead-magnet PDF -> an email list (Kit), which is
the actual long-term asset being built.

## Repo structure

```
main/               Daily quote/fact pipeline (163+ entries)
  content.json      The content library: id, type (quote/fact), text,
                     attribution, source, used, date_used
  state.json        {"cursor": N} - index into content.json for "what's next"
  select_next.py    Picks the next unused entry from cursor, wraps around
  post_all.py       Posts to Instagram (video) + X/Threads/Pinterest (Buffer)
  update_state.py   Marks entry used + advances cursor (gated on Instagram
                     actually succeeding - see GOTCHAS below)
  pinterest_seo.py  Builds keyword-rich Pinterest titles/descriptions
                     (Pinterest ranks on these, NOT hashtags - ~1% weight)
  board_router.py   Routes each pin to the best-matching one of 9 Pinterest
                     boards based on philosopher/topic

editorial/          Twice-weekly long-form carousel pipeline (52+ entries)
  content.json      id, title, label, body, cta, hashtags, used, date_used,
                     pinterest_hook
  render_essay.py   Multi-slide carousel renderer, auto-paginates, CTA gets
                     its own dedicated final slide (not squeezed onto body)
  render_pinterest_teaser.py  Pinterest gets a DELIBERATELY INCOMPLETE teaser
                     image (cuts off mid-scene) with the pin's destination
                     link set to the actual Instagram post - drives
                     click-through rather than duplicating content
  post_all.py       Same platform-posting pattern as main/

reminders/          Self-monitoring, emails devdave666@gmail.com when:
  check_and_remind.py   - Instagram token nearing 60-day expiry (5-day warn)
                         - either content pool drops below 10 unused entries
                           (includes a ready-to-paste prompt for topping up)
  check_missed_post.py  Runs 4hrs after normal schedule; if NO post went out
                         today, auto-triggers a recovery run AND emails you
  send_email.py     Generic mailer, Gmail SMTP + app password

links/              Self-hosted link-in-bio page (replaces Linktree)
  index.html        Single-file HTML/CSS/JS. Deployed via Vercel, connected
                     to this GitHub repo (auto-deploys on push to this
                     folder specifically - Root Directory is set to `links`
                     in Vercel's project settings, NOT the repo root)

composite_card.py   Shared image renderer for main/ pipeline's statue+quote
                     cards. IMAGE_MAP maps philosopher names to background
                     files in backgrounds/. Non-philosopher facts use a
                     single fixed "psychology2.jpg" background.

backgrounds/         ~28 statue/abstract images (1080x1344, dark aesthetic)
fonts/                IBM Plex Serif (Regular, Bold, BoldItalic) - the only
                      typeface used anywhere in this project
pins/, videos/        Generated output, committed by the workflows themselves

.github/workflows/
  main-daily-post.yml       Daily, 13:00 UTC nominal (GitHub's scheduler is
                            unreliable - see GOTCHAS)
  editorial-post.yml        Mon/Thu
  missed-post-check.yml     Daily, 17:00 UTC - the self-healing safety net
  generate-content.yml      LEGACY - was Make.com's dispatch target before
                            full migration off Make. Should be dormant/unused
                            now but has not been deleted. If you see it
                            firing, something is wrong (Make should be fully
                            deleted, not just deactivated - deactivating
                            alone was proven unreliable once already).
```

## External services and how access works

**GitHub Secrets** (the automated pipelines' only credential source):
`INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `INSTAGRAM_USER_ID`, `BUFFER_API_KEY`,
`BUFFER_X_CHANNEL_ID`, `BUFFER_THREADS_CHANNEL_ID`,
`BUFFER_PINTEREST_CHANNEL_ID`, `BUFFER_PINTEREST_BOARD_ID`,
`GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD`, `REMINDER_EMAIL_TO`, `REMINDER_EMAIL_FROM`.
These are write-only once set - nobody (including Claude) can read them back
out. The automated workflows already have everything they need; you do not
need any of this to just let the pipeline keep running.

**Instagram**: direct Graph API calls (graph.instagram.com), no
third-party tool. Token expires ~60 days, the reminders/ system emails a
warning starting 5 days out.

**Buffer**: direct GraphQL API (api.buffer.com) for X, Threads, Pinterest.
NOT using Buffer's official app connectors - raw HTTP calls with a personal
API key, built this way early on due to feature limitations in Buffer's own
UI flow for this use case.

**Vercel**: hosts the links/ page, connected via GitHub integration (auto
deploy on push). Also has an MCP connector available to Claude, but that
MCP tool (`deploy_to_vercel`) has a hard, confirmed limitation: it can only
successfully create ONE deployment per project - every subsequent deploy
through that specific tool gets a 403 permission error, even as Owner, even
with Deployment Protection off. The GitHub-integration auto-deploy route
does not have this limitation and is the reliable path for ongoing updates.

**Make.com**: intentionally NOT used anywhere anymore. It caused enough
real incidents (silently-still-active scenario reposting stale content
daily for an unknown period, error-handling that swallowed failures, the
2-free-scenario cap making testing painful) that it was fully deleted, not
just deactivated. Do not reintroduce it without a very good reason.

**Image generation**: Black Forest Labs direct API (api.bfl.ai), not
Replicate. Endpoint is `flux-pro-1.1` for from-scratch generation (needs
explicit width/height in pixels - its `aspect_ratio` param is unreliable
and silently falls back to 1024x768 default) or `flux-2-pro` for
reference-image-guided editing (`input_image` param accepts a URL directly).
Reference-image editing was what actually solved a stuck compositional
problem after multiple pure-text-prompt attempts failed - worth remembering
as a technique, not just a one-off fix.

**Kit** (email/lead magnet): `https://thb.kit.com/ac3784a0f7` is the live
landing page for the free guide PDF ("The Evidence-Based Stoic"). No API
integration - this is just a link target, not something Claude posts to
programmatically.

## What a NEW AI session needs from the human to actually operate this

The automated pipelines need **nothing** - they already run via GitHub
Secrets. A new AI session only needs credentials if the human wants it to
do things beyond what's automated: manual/one-off posting, debugging a live
incident, adding content that requires direct API calls, extending the
pipeline, etc.

MCP-connected tools (Buffer, Make if reconnected, Vercel, Gmail, Notion,
Canva, etc.) persist at the Claude account level - a new chat should already
have these available without the human doing anything, IF the human is on
the same Claude account. Check the tool list before assuming you don't have
something.

Raw API tokens shared as plain text earlier in conversation (Instagram
access token, Buffer personal API key, GitHub PAT, BFL key, Gmail app
password) are NOT automatically available in a new chat - they only exist
in that conversation's own context. If you need one and don't have it,
ask the human directly rather than guessing or trying to extract it from
GitHub Secrets (which is write-only and will not work).

A GitHub PAT with repo write access is the single most useful thing to get
early, since almost everything in this project is "edit a file, commit,
push" - the workflows pick it up from there.

## Hard-won lessons (read before repeating these mistakes)

- **GitHub Actions' `schedule:` trigger is genuinely unreliable** on the
  free tier - it can fire hours late, or (rarely) not fire at all. Build
  around this (see missed-post-check.yml) rather than trusting it.
- **Instagram's container processing can fail transiently.** A fresh retry
  of the exact same unmodified file has resolved this every time it's been
  observed. Both post_all.py scripts now auto-retry 3x before giving up.
- **A failing secondary platform (X/Threads/Pinterest) must never block
  the others or prevent the state update.** Each platform call is wrapped
  independently. State only advances if Instagram (the primary platform)
  specifically succeeded - gated on an explicit `_instagram_success.txt`
  marker file, not on the overall step's exit code.
- **X has a hard 280-character limit.** Editorial captions (longer intro
  paragraphs + CTA + hashtags) can exceed this even when the main daily
  quotes never do. Both pipelines now build a separately-truncated X
  caption rather than assuming the main caption always fits.
- **When Claude tests and the human approves a change, ACTUALLY COMMIT
  AND PUSH IT.** This has already gone wrong once (a handle-styling fix
  was tested, approved, shown to the human as "done" - and never actually
  pushed, so it silently didn't apply to a week of live posts before
  anyone noticed). Verify against `git log` or the raw GitHub file after
  every "fix", don't trust local state alone.
- **Composition/scale problems in generated images are much better solved
  by passing a known-good image as a reference** (flux-2-pro's `input_image`)
  than by iterating on text-only prompts. But be precise about what you
  want preserved (scale/framing/lighting) vs. changed (subject identity) -
  an early attempt preserved way more of the reference's actual identity
  than intended, producing something that just looked like the reference
  image with a texture change instead of a genuinely distinct subject.
- **Don't assume a background task like `deploy_to_vercel` can be called
  repeatedly.** It can't, past the first call per project. Prefer the
  GitHub-integration auto-deploy path for anything that will need updating.
- **The old Make scenario was "deactivated" once and it didn't hold** -
  it silently kept running and duplicate-posting for an unknown period.
  It has since been fully deleted. If anything resembling Make.com
  automation reappears in this project's behavior, investigate immediately
  rather than assuming it's been handled.
- **`continue-on-error: true` hides failures from the GitHub UI at a
  glance** - the step shows green even when the underlying script failed,
  by design (that's the point of continue-on-error). This means you cannot
  tell from the Actions tab's checkmarks alone whether a run actually
  posted anything; you have to check content.json's date_used or the raw
  logs. Discovered 2026-08-10 when Instagram failed 3 consecutive attempts
  (not just once) and every single step still showed "success."
- **A "commit rendered output" step with no guard for a no-op render can
  permanently deadlock a pipeline.** The "Commit state update" step already
  had an `if git diff --cached --quiet; then ... exit 0` guard for the case
  where Instagram failed and state was correctly left unchanged - but the
  earlier "Commit rendered images/assets" step didn't. When Instagram fails
  after a successful render+commit, the next scheduled run re-selects and
  re-renders the *same* entry (state never advanced), producing byte-identical
  output with nothing new to commit. Under `bash -e` that `git commit` then
  fails outright, killing the job before it ever reaches the posting step
  again - a permanent loop that only manual intervention breaks. This is
  exactly what happened to editorial: stuck from 2026-08-06 (Instagram
  fetch-timing failure) through 2026-08-13 (three straight hard failures at
  the commit step) until fixed. Both `main-daily-post.yml` and
  `editorial-post.yml` now guard the render-commit step the same way the
  state-commit step already was. If a similarly-shaped commit step is added
  anywhere in this project, give it the same guard from the start.
- **Don't send a "recovered" email before verifying the recovery actually
  worked.** check_missed_post.py used to fire the "Recovered" email
  immediately after triggering a recovery dispatch, without checking
  whether that dispatch's run actually succeeded. On 2026-08-10 it sent
  "Recovered" while the auto-triggered recovery run had also failed
  (Instagram was down longer than the 3-attempt retry window). Fixed to
  actually poll the triggered run to completion and report its real
  outcome before emailing anything.
- **Copyright/quote authenticity matters here specifically.** This account's
  whole differentiator is evidence-based rigor (explicitly stated in the
  lead magnet PDF). Verify philosopher quotes are real and correctly
  attributed before adding them - several widely-circulated ones are fake.
  Same bar applies to psychology claims: state evidence strength honestly,
  don't oversell popular claims that have weak support.

## Current experimental work

Branch `feature/kinetic-tts` (NOT merged to main, main is untouched and
safe): building word-synced kinetic text animation using Kokoro-82M
(free, Apache 2.0, CPU-capable TTS) + WhisperX (word-level forced alignment)
to replace the current static text cards with word-by-word reveal timed to
narration. As of last update: TTS generation works, voice selection is
still being tuned (the human wants more "authority/sage" quality and less
robotic monotone delivery than Kokoro's default prosody gives), timing/
alignment step not yet built. Do not merge anything from this branch to
main without the human explicitly confirming it's ready.

## Tone/brand notes worth preserving

Dark background (#0A0A0A-ish), gold accent (#B8862E / brighter #DEB26E for
small text needing more visibility - the brand gold reads too dark at small
sizes), IBM Plex Serif exclusively. Bio line: "Ancient intuition. Modern
proof." CTAs across the editorial pipeline are deliberately low-stakes
invitations ("comment one word") rather than anything asking someone to
publicly expose a vulnerability - this was a deliberate correction from an
earlier, worse CTA style. The human has explicitly declined content that
overclaims pop-psychology/self-diagnosis framing (e.g. "if X bothers you,
you might have OCD/ADHD") even when it would likely perform well, because
it contradicts the account's evidence-based positioning - respect this if
asked for similar content again.
